parts.move: state Newton's law of gravitation with the meaning of each symbol
parts.prompt: State Newton's law of gravitation for two point masses, defining each symbol.
scheme: F = Gm₁m₂/r²
G is the gravitational constant, m₁ and m₂ the masses, r their centre-to-centre separation
The force is always attractive, acting along the line joining the two masses
parts.answer: Newton's law of gravitation is F = Gm₁m₂/r², where G is the gravitational constant, m₁ and m₂ are the point masses and r is their separation. The force is always attractive and acts along the line joining the centres.

parts.move: state Coulomb's law and the sign rule that decides attraction or repulsion
parts.prompt: State Coulomb's law for two point charges, and state how the sign of the charges determines the direction of the force.
scheme: F = Q₁Q₂/(4πε₀r²)
Q₁ and Q₂ are the charges, r their separation, ε₀ the permittivity of free space
Like charges (same sign) repel; unlike charges (opposite signs) attract
parts.answer: Coulomb's law gives F = Q₁Q₂/(4πε₀r²), where Q₁ and Q₂ are the point charges, r their separation and ε₀ the permittivity of free space. The force is repulsive between like charges and attractive between unlike charges.

parts.move: compare the shared inverse-square structure of the two force laws and their differences in sign behaviour and strength
parts.prompt: Newton's law of gravitation and Coulomb's law are both inverse-square laws. State the structural feature they share and explain two ways their forms differ.
scheme: Shared: both forces act along the line joining the centres and vary as 1/r² with the product of the two source quantities (mass or charge)
Difference in sign behaviour: gravitation is always attractive, while the electric force attracts for unlike charges and repels for like charges
Difference in strength: the constants differ enormously, so between charged particles the electric force vastly exceeds the gravitational one
Gravity therefore accumulates with matter, whereas electric forces between neutral bodies cancel
parts.answer: Both laws have the same structure — force proportional to the product of two intrinsic quantities divided by the square of the separation, directed along the line joining the centres. They differ in sign behaviour: gravity only attracts, while electric forces attract or repel according to the charge signs; and in strength: the electric constant is some 40 orders of magnitude larger than G, so electric forces dominate between charged particles.

parts.move: reject linear distance scaling in favour of the inverse-square relation for force laws
parts.prompt: A student says: 'If I double the distance between two charges, the force between them halves, because the force decreases with distance.' Explain the error and state the correct factor by which the force changes.
scheme: Coulomb's law gives F ∝ 1/r², not 1/r
Doubling r reduces the force by 2² = 4, so the force becomes one quarter of its previous value
Conversely halving the distance would increase the force fourfold
parts.answer: The force falls as the inverse square of the separation, not linearly with distance. Doubling the separation quarters the force (F/4), and halving it would make the force four times larger.

parts.move: apply both force laws to the same pair of protons and argue from the constant ratio which dominates
parts.prompt: A student asks why the nucleus is held together by the strong nuclear force rather than by gravity, given that two protons also attract each other gravitationally. Using the constants in Newton's and Coulomb's laws, explain which force dominates between two protons and why.
scheme: For two protons at any separation, the electric repulsion exceeds the gravitational attraction by a factor of about 10³⁶
The Coulomb constant (≈9×10⁹ N m² C⁻²) is about 40 orders of magnitude larger than G (≈6.7×10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²)
Gravity is utterly negligible at nuclear scale, so only the strong nuclear force can bind protons against the electric repulsion
parts.answer: Between two protons the electric repulsion is roughly 10³⁶ times stronger than their gravitational attraction, because the Coulomb constant is about forty orders of magnitude larger than G for comparable charge and mass values. Gravity is far too weak to bind a nucleus, so the strong nuclear force must overcome the electric repulsion instead.

parts.move: justify why neutrality of bulk matter lets the weaker gravity dominate at astronomical scale
parts.prompt: The electric attraction between an electron and a proton is some 10³⁹ times stronger than their gravitational attraction. Yet planetary motion is governed entirely by gravity. Explain why gravity, not electrostatics, controls the orbits of stars and planets.
scheme: Bulk matter is electrically neutral: the numbers of protons and electrons balance, so the net charge — and hence the net electric force — between astronomical bodies is essentially zero
Mass has no negative counterpart, so gravitational attraction always accumulates with the amount of matter present
Electric forces between neutral bodies cancel, leaving gravity as the only long-range force that shapes orbits despite being weaker between individual particles
parts.answer: Stars and planets contain equal numbers of protons and electrons, so their net charge is effectively zero and the electrostatic force between them cancels away. Gravity has no such cancellation — it always accumulates with total mass — so the far weaker gravitational force ends up governing orbital motion.

parts.move: equate Coulomb's law potential to the incoming kinetic energy to find the distance of closest approach
parts.prompt: An alpha particle with kinetic energy 5.0×10⁻¹³ J is fired directly at a gold nucleus (charge +79e) and is momentarily at rest at its closest approach. Calculate the separation at closest approach. (e = 1.60×10⁻¹⁹ C, 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99×10⁹ N m² C⁻²)
scheme: At the closest approach all kinetic energy has become electric potential energy: E = Q₁Q₂/(4πε₀r)
Q₁ = 2e and Q₂ = 79e, so Q₁Q₂ = 158 × (1.60×10⁻¹⁹)² = 4.05×10⁻³⁶ C²
parts.answer: At the turning point the 5.0×10⁻¹³ J of kinetic energy has converted entirely into electric potential energy, so r = Q₁Q₂/(4πε₀E) = (8.99×10⁹ × 158 × (1.60×10⁻¹⁹)²)/(5.0×10⁻¹³) ≈ 7.3×10⁻¹⁴ m.

parts.move: derive the escape speed by equating kinetic energy to the gravitational potential from Newton's law
parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed a rocket must be given to escape Earth's gravitational field from the surface, ignoring air resistance. (M_E = 5.97×10²⁴ kg, R_E = 6.37×10⁶ m, G = 6.67×10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²)
scheme: Escape requires kinetic energy equal to the depth of the gravitational potential well: ½mv² = GMm/R
The rocket's own mass cancels, giving v = √(2GM/R)
= 1.1×10⁴ m s⁻¹ (about 11 km s⁻¹)
parts.answer: Escape speed satisfies ½mv² = GMm/R, from Newton's law of gravitation, so v = √(2GM/R) = √(2×6.67×10⁻¹¹×5.97×10²⁴/6.37×10⁶) ≈ 1.1×10⁴ m s⁻¹ — the familiar 11 km s⁻¹, independent of the rocket's mass.
